title: TAPPaaS Site
description: The Site is the top-level umbrella for a TAPPaaS installation (ADR-007d). It holds site-wide identity, its locations (the primary one is where it is), backup target, update schedule, module catalog repositories, and references to the organization config files. The cluster's nodes are not listed here either: they are their pvehost instances (config/<node>.json). Environments are NOT listed here — they are simply whatever is present under config/environments/*.json (enumerated from the directory, not from site.json). Domain, DNS, and identity are per-environment (NOT site-wide) and live in config/environments/*.json. site.json replaces configuration.json at cutover; during the phased migration both files may coexist. See ADR-007 P2.

location.description: A place: where devices stand, or where another site is.

name.description: The location's name: how devices, rooms and backup peers name it. It is the record's key.
name.changeNote: Devices, rooms and backup peers name it: add the new location, point them at it, delete this one.

kind.description: site: a place of this site's own equipment — its building, a provider's data centre. remote: another site's place, a backup buddy's.

city.description: The city — lets an off-site copy in the same country show it is elsewhere.

address.description: The street address, or the provider and data centre — for an off-site copy in the same city.

timezone.description: IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Copenhagen). Required on the primary location: it is the site's.

latitude.description: Decimal degrees, north positive. Set by the operator — no node knows it. Read by modules that need a position rather than a country (Home Assistant's core config).

longitude.description: Decimal degrees, east positive. Set by the operator — no node knows it.

name.description: Neutral site code (e.g. warmelo1 — place plus number). Aligned with the Proxmox cluster name at creation, informational afterwards (ADR-007d #426). Not used to name any environment, organization, or zone — those key on defaultEnvironment.
name.changeNote: The site's code, given when the site was created and aligned with its Proxmox cluster's name then. Nothing renames the cluster, so the two would no longer match.

defaultEnvironment.description: Name of the default (tenant) environment — also its network zone and owner organization. Decoupled from the site code so site.name can be renamed with a single edit without touching any environment/org/zone (ADR-007d #426). Must be a valid zone/environment slug.
defaultEnvironment.changeNote: The install created the default environment, its zone and its owner organization under this name, and renamed srv to it. Pointing it at another name would leave those behind under the old one.

email.description: Installer/admin contact email (Let's Encrypt ACME account, people bootstrap). Carried over from configuration.json .tappaas.email during the S3b reader cutover.

version.description: The TAPPaaS release this site was installed from, written once by create-site.sh. Not the version it runs: that is read from the checkout (git describe; site-manager site show, ADR-028 D13).
version.changeNote: Written once when the site was created: the release it was installed from. The release it runs is read from the checkout.

locations.description: Every place the site's devices can be, and every place this site cares about, by name: its own building, a provider's data centre, a backup buddy's site. The site's own is primaryLocation. A device, room or backup peer names one; the address is read from here.
locations.changeNote: Has verbs of its own: site-manager location add, modify, delete.

primaryLocation.description: The location the site is at, and the one a device is at when it names none. Its timezone is the site's: every node and guest is set to it.

locale.description: POSIX locale (e.g. en_US), as set on the first node. Site-wide: it does not move with a location.

keyboard.description: Console keyboard layout (e.g. dk), as set on the first node — its XKBLAYOUT. The PXE answer file and every OS family read it from here. Site-wide: it does not move with a location.

location.description: RETIRED — replaced by locations, primaryLocation, locale and keyboard; never write this field. Retained so a site.json migration 0019 has not reached is classified rather than reported unknown; site-manager validate refuses it, and readers still read it until the migration has run.
location.changeNote: Retired: migration 0019 moves it into locations.

network.description: Site WAN configuration. No rootDomain — domains are per-environment.

isp.description: ISP name, for operator reference only.

publicIp.description: Public IP address, or "auto" to discover at runtime.

wan.description: How the firewall's WAN gets its addresses (ADR-030 D2). Converged by the network update; a WAN edited by hand in OPNsense is drift and is put back. Absent: IPv4 by DHCP and, when ipv6 is true, IPv6 dynamic.

address.description: static: the WAN address in CIDR form, e.g. 198.51.100.10/24.

ipv6.description: dynamic (default when ipv6 is true): DHCPv6 and a delegated prefix of prefixLength. static: a fixed WAN address and the prefix the ISP routes to it. none: no IPv6 on the WAN. The site prefix must be /56 or larger (ADR-030 D3).

prefixLength.description: dynamic: the delegated prefix size to ask for, 48-56.

address.description: static: the WAN address in CIDR form, e.g. 2001:db8:0:1::2/64.

prefix.description: static: the prefix routed to the WAN address, /56 or larger, e.g. 2001:db8:6648::/48.

hardware.description: RETIRED — the cluster's nodes are their pvehost instances (config/<node>.json), each with its storagePools; never write this field. Retained so a site.json migration 0022 has not reached is classified rather than reported unknown; site-manager validate refuses it, and the node readers still read it until the migration has run.
hardware.changeNote: Retired: migration 0022 moves each node's storagePools onto its pvehost instance. The nodes have verbs of their own: site-manager node add, node delete.

backup.description: Site-wide backup target. null when no backup is configured yet.

defaultRetention.description: Site-wide default backup retention period (e.g. 7y, 5y, 1y). The base of the Site -> Environment -> Module retention cascade (ADR-007 P9): environments and modules may override it.

offsiteResidency.description: Data residency of the offsite backup buddy (ADR-007 P9). Used by 'backup-manager validate' to reject backing an eu-only environment up to a non-EU offsite. eu-only by default; set global only when the offsite is outside the EU.

defaultSchedule.description: Site-wide default backup frequency and the base of the Site -> Environment -> Module schedule cascade (ADR-012 §3.2). One of 'daily' | 'weekly' | 'monthly', or a bare 'HH:MM' meaning daily at that time. Environments and modules may override it, but never with anything more frequent than once a day — that ceiling is the platform's, not a policy.

updateSchedule.description: Site-wide update schedule (ADR-017 D7). {frequency: none|daily|weekly|monthly, weekday: day name, hour: 0-23}. weekday is read only under weekly and monthly; hour defaults to 2. The legacy [period, day, hour] triple is still read, and migration 0003 rewrites it.

weekday.description: The day it runs on, under weekly and monthly.

channel.description: Which release channel this site takes, and therefore how much risk it accepts (ADR-028 D9). `unstable` is where development is proven, `staging` soaks a revision under real use for one boundary, `production` is what everyone else runs. The channel is a promise about risk; the branch each repository tracks is where the code sits — they are expected to agree (TAPPaaS: unstable=main, staging=staging, production=stable) and `site-manager` warns when they do not.
channel.note: Changing it is allowed in both directions, but moving towards production takes the site to OLDER code: `site modify --channel` warns and requires --force, because ADR-025 config migrations are forward-only and a site that has applied a migration cannot run code that predates it.

automaticReboot.description: Whether updates may reboot automatically. Site-wide until P3 (then moves to Environment).

ipv6.description: Whether this site runs IPv6 next to IPv4, applied by the network module's update. True: the firewall allows IPv6, takes a prefix from the WAN (network.wan.ipv6) and gives every zone with an ipv6Subnet its /64. False: no zone has IPv6, and the firewall drops all IPv6 and Unbound resolves over IPv4 only. See network-manager/IPV6.md.
ipv6.note: Set it true only when the upstream provides IPv6. Changing it reloads the firewall's filter and Unbound once; IPv4 traffic is not interrupted.

dnssec.description: Whether the firewall's resolver (Unbound) validates DNSSEC, applied by the network module's update. True: answers for signed domains are validated and a forged or broken answer is refused (SERVFAIL). The site's own names are not affected: the internal domain and private reverse zones are marked insecure, and the split-horizon answers for published names are local data.
dnssec.note: Turn it off only if an upstream path breaks DNSSEC (a middlebox that strips signatures). Changing it reloads Unbound once.

branding.description: The site's own look on its sign-in page (Authentik). logo: an image file (svg, png, jpg or webp, at most 2 MB) shown above the login form in place of the logo generated from displayName; logoDark: a variant for the dark theme, of the same file type (absent: logo serves both). Paths are relative to the config directory. Applied by the identity module's update.
branding.note: Without branding the logo is generated: the site's displayName with "powered by TAPPaaS" beneath, in a light and a dark variant. A missing file leaves the login page as it is and says so.

logo.description: The sign-in page's logo: an svg, png, jpg or webp file of at most 2 MB, relative to the config directory.

logoDark.description: Its variant for the dark theme, of the same file type (absent: logo serves both).

dnsBlocklists.description: DNS blocklists the firewall's resolver applies, by the network module's update. Absent: none. lists are OPNsense's blocklist codes (atf = abuse.ch ThreatFox, hgz011 = hagezi threat intelligence, oisd1 = OISD big, ag = AdGuard, ...); zones limits filtering to those zones' clients, IPv4 and IPv6 (none listed: every client); allow names domains never blocked. A blocked name answers NXDOMAIN.
dnsBlocklists.note: Service zones are best left out: their modules fetch updates, images and models, and a false positive there fails an update. A change takes effect as cached answers expire (minutes). An unknown list code is refused with the codes the firewall offers.

lists.description: OPNsense's blocklist codes (atf, hgz011, oisd1, ag, ...). None: no blocking.

zones.description: The zones whose clients are filtered (none listed: every client).

diskAutoGrow.description: Automatic disk growth: on every module update, a VM whose / is at or over threshold % full has its disk grown by growPercent % (at least minGrowGB), if the disk's pool — on the guest's node and on its HA replica node — stays at or under poolCeiling % used. Absent: on, with the defaults shown. A module opts out with diskAutoGrow: false and caps growth with diskSizeMax.
diskAutoGrow.note: Linux VMs only; a container's disk is grown by hand. A grow without room prints a DEFERRED: line the update summary collects. Pool use is Proxmox's (pvesm status), which counts a thick disk's full size.

threshold.description: Grow a VM's disk when its / is at or over this % full.

growPercent.description: Grow it by this % of its size.

minGrowGB.description: …and by at least this many GB.

poolCeiling.description: Only while the disk's pool, on the guest's node and its HA replica's, stays at or under this % used.

snapshotRetention.description: Number of snapshots to retain. Site-wide until P3 (then moves to Environment).

repositories.description: Registry of checked-out repositories whose module catalogs back NAME-based module resolution (resolve-module.sh, ADR-004). This is NOT the only way a module is located and NOT required for a module to work: install-module.sh takes the current directory first, recording the module's source dir as .location in its deployed config, so a module installed from an unregistered path resolves through .location alone (issue #460).

branch.description: Branch tracked by the local checkout.

path.description: Absolute path of the local checkout. Load-bearing: resolve-module.sh skips any entry without it, so a repository lacking path contributes no modules to name-based resolution. Not in `required` only so site.json files written before it was declared still validate.

managed.description: full = the repository carries TAPPaaS modules and its catalog is validated on add; tracked = registered without catalog requirements.

catalog.description: Module catalog path, relative to the repository root. Written by `repository add` as the path it actually found (which may be the legacy src/modules.json) and read by resolve-module.sh. Absent means: try src/module-catalog.json, then legacy src/modules.json.

trust.description: The fingerprints of the keys the repository's owners sign its releases with (ADR-033 D5) — from them, out of band, never from the repository. A fresh clone runs nothing to take its signers from, so the current release on a staging or production branch must be signed by one of these keys, which that release's own .tappaas/allowed_signers lists; from then on the site verifies each update against the signers of the release it last verified (config/.trust/<name>.json). `repository introduce` checks the checkout against them again at any time. Written by the installer for the TAPPaaS repository and by `repository add --signer` for others. Absent: the repository was added with --unsigned, or predates ADR-033 and verifies from the revision it runs. When the owners' keys change, put their new fingerprints here.

signers.description: SHA-256 fingerprints, as ssh-keygen -l prints them (SHA256:...). Any one of them may have signed the current release. For TAPPaaS they are published in INSTALL.md.

repositories.changeNote: Has verbs of its own: site-manager repository add, modify, delete.

requireSigned.description: Refuse to update a repository on the staging or production channel unless it signs its releases (ADR-033 D9). false (the default): a repository that lists no signing keys in .tappaas/allowed_signers still updates, and the health check reports it as unsigned. A repository that does list keys is always verified, whatever this says.
requireSigned.note: Turn it on when the site must show that everything it runs comes from signed releases. Unstable branches are never signed and are not affected.
